chapter: Biddle, Durham and early road shows
title: Playing the minstrel show with J. L. Cronan's carnival
summary: The trombonist wired a 42-car carnival, and Randolph played ballyhoo in town to draw crowds, nearly laughing at the barker's closing line.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I sent her back home in Durham. Well, the show broke up and after that we went to look in the paper and we saw J. L. Cronan's Carnival Show where they needed a band. So, Holt wired them -- the trombone player wired them, so we went there and we joined them in Burlington, North Carolina. And that's where we played for the -- see, this was a 42-car carnival and we played the minstrel part. And, of
course, every evening we would have to go out in the town and play to draw the crowd and (unintelligible) The man would spiel

Yes. So, the man would -- he would give -- this was comical, because he would give this speech and as soon as he said this punch word, then I'm supposed to hit right in to it, see. Well, the man said it so funny, you can't play and laugh -- not a trumpet, see. He would say -- now, here's his line, "Now, ladies and gentlemen, if you come and see our little show, we have --," he would tell about the girls we had on the show, so many girls, and the comedians, "and we want you to come end enjoy yourself and then you knock on everyone's door and tell them about this show. (But) Ladies and Gentlemen," now, this is what would get me, "if you come and you don't like the show, please don't knock."

And when he said that -- as soon as he said, "please don't knock," I got to say ra-da-da-da- -- that was something. So, I left that show for a while. I stayed there for awhile and I left them and went to Durham -- back to Durham and played in a fellow by the name of Watkins -- he owned a theater there. And I went there and took over the leadership of the band there.
